rubrics.rubric: Does Data_Validation_Report.xlsx provide a complete cell-level validation record in the required structure?
criterion: The workbook has exactly the sheets Error_Classification, Coding_Discrepancies, and Summary_Matrix.
Error_Classification contains the required columns Row, Responder_ID, Column, Error_Type, Current_Value, Reference_Data_Comparison, and Recommended_Action.
Every flagged cell has its own row rather than being represented only by a pattern example.
Every missing value is flagged with a handling recommendation.
Duplicate identifiers and logical inconsistencies required by the codebook are documented.
Row references are defined clearly enough to locate the corresponding raw record.

rubrics.rubric: Are validation findings and error classifications grounded in the codebook and reference datasets?
criterion: Every raw value is checked against the applicable codebook values, ranges, or rules.
Reference_Data_Comparison uses the matching respondent, organizational, or time-management record when available.
Typo, Impossible Value, Missing Value, and Coding Inconsistency are used consistently with the documented evidence.
Legitimate Outlier is used only when the value is plausible and confirmed by a reference dataset.
A source-consistent value that violates a codebook rule is distinguished from a raw-entry transcription error.
Recommended actions preserve uncertainty when the codebook and reference source disagree.

rubrics.rubric: Do Coding_Discrepancies and Summary_Matrix accurately summarize the validation work?
criterion: Coding_Discrepancies contains one row per variable whose raw coding differs from the expected coding.
Each coding-discrepancy row shows the raw scheme, expected scheme, affected rows or count, and recommended recode.
Summary_Matrix cross-tabulates Error_Type by Demographic, Organizational, and Time-related category.
Summary_Matrix row, column, and grand totals reconcile with Error_Classification.

rubrics.rubric: Does the executed notebook create and validate the required merged analysis dataset?
criterion: The notebook merges time_management.csv, organizational_data.csv, and respondents.csv on responder_id.
Record counts are shown before and after each merge.
Unmatched or duplicated merge keys are reported.
The notebook applies and documents the cleaning or exclusion decisions used for analysis.
All analysis cells are executed and their outputs are visible.

rubrics.rubric: Does the notebook correctly reconcile the survey productivity distribution with the published benchmark?
criterion: Productivity responses are collapsed into more productive, equally productive, and less productive using the instructed mapping.
The survey percentages are calculated from the cleaned time-management data with the denominator shown.
The comparison uses the published 64 percent, 22 percent, and 14 percent values.
Variance is reported as survey percentage minus PDF percentage in percentage points.
At least two substantive methodological explanations for the benchmark difference are provided.
Explanations are framed as plausible interpretations rather than hidden expected conclusions.

rubrics.rubric: Does the notebook perform and report all three required chi-square analyses correctly?
criterion: A chi-square test is performed for productivity by organization_size.
A chi-square test is performed for productivity by metro_or_regional.
A chi-square test is performed for productivity by manage_others.
Each test reports chi-square statistic, degrees of freedom, and p-value.
Contingency-table construction and any category consolidation or sparse-cell limitation are documented.
Interpretations distinguish association from causation.

rubrics.rubric: Does Policy_Briefing_Package.docx follow the required four-section structure and accurately communicate the analysis?
criterion: The document has the four required section headings in the required order.
Section 1 is no more than 200 words and names at least three concrete validation patterns.

Section 2 includes the required benchmark-comparison columns and separate More productive, Equally productive, and Less productive rows, each with the PDF value, cleaned-survey value, percentage-point variance, and a plausible explanation.
Section 2 values and explanations agree with the notebook.
Section 3 translates all three chi-square findings into plain language.
Section 4 contains three to five methodological caveats derived from the validation and analysis.

rubrics.rubric: Are the comparison visualization and all three deliverables complete and integrated?
criterion: The executed notebook contains a grouped comparison chart for the PDF and survey productivity distributions.
The chart labels both data sources and makes the percentage-point discrepancies visible.
At least one chart generated by the notebook is embedded in the Word document.
All three exact filenames and required formats are present.
Workbook counts, notebook cleaning decisions, and briefing statements are mutually consistent.
